evals.name: challenger-eval-1
evals.expected_output: Teach is Covered, citing the reframe about the two-to-three hour stale-information gap after a manual update, and Ravi reacting with surprise about last week's mis-pick. Tailor is Covered, citing Sam naming Priya specifically and connecting the fix to her not being blamed for gaps. Take control is Missed, citing Sam accepting Ravi's end-of-September timeline and under-$15k budget with no pushback or tradeoff. The pitch-arc check shows Warmer and Reframe present, Rational drowning and New way skipped, and the call jumping close to Our solution once timeline/budget came up. Closes with a single biggest missed teaching opportunity, likely the unchallenged timeline or budget moment.
expectations: Teach, Tailor, and Take control each receive a Status
Teach is scored Covered and cites the reframe about the stale-information gap after a schedule update, not just the manual-update pain itself
Tailor is scored Covered or Partial and cites Sam naming Priya and her specific exposure to blame
Take control is scored Missed or Partial, citing that Sam agreed to the timeline and budget without any pushback or tradeoff
The commercial-teaching pitch arc lists which of the six steps appeared and flags that Rational drowning and New way were skipped
Closes with a single named biggest missed teaching opportunity, not a full recap
Cites at least one specific, concrete detail from the transcript (a name, number, or quoted phrase) rather than a generic paraphrase that could apply to any call

evals.name: challenger-eval-2-reads-well-too
evals.prompt: run challenger on a transcript of a short first discovery call that, by any reasonable read, went well for a call at that early stage even though it never reached rational drowning or emotional impact
evals.expected_output: The pitch-arc steps the call had no room to reach (typically Rational drowning, Emotional impact, New way) are marked Not applicable rather than Missed. Teach is scored on whether the Reframe step that did happen carried genuine insight, not penalized for the call's short length. The audit does not read as mostly Missed just because the call didn't complete the full six-step arc.
expectations: Pitch-arc steps unreachable at this call's stage are marked Not applicable, not Missed
A genuinely strong short call is not scored as mostly Missed
The reads-well-too check from references/rubric.md is applied before the audit is finalized

evals.name: challenger-eval-3-csv
evals.prompt: run challenger on a CRM pipeline export csv with deal rows that have no teaching insight or point-of-view field logged
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a structural hygiene sweep, not a call-quality audit, and says so explicitly. Flags each deal row with no logged teaching moment or point-of-view field populated. Output is a table sorted by deal value descending. Makes no claim about what was actually taught on any specific call from CRM fields alone.
expectations: States explicitly that CSV mode is a structural check, not a call-quality claim
Flags rows with no logged teaching moment or insight field
Output is sorted by deal value descending
Does not claim to know what was actually taught on any specific call from CRM fields alone
